chapter: Brown's Band in Chicago and New York
title: Where the word jazz came from and Swor and Mack
summary: Loyacano's account of jazz as a word at Lamb's and how the comedians Swor and Mack helped the band catch on.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, uh, down the street, in the middle of the block, was the, uh, I'd say, I think it was Cones Grand Opera House. That was big time Waterville. And Bert Swann and Charlie Mack came to town. And so they came over there to hear this jazzy band. Incidentally, that's where that word jazz came from. Ah. Jazzy band. Clangy, jazzy, anything. Who put it on y'all? Do you remember? Well, who knows? It just grew up around Randolph and York. Were you in Chicago before y'all? No, no. They didn't even know how to spell it. They first spelled it J-A-Z, then J-A-Z-Z, then J-A-S, and J-A-S-S. And it finally stuck and was recognized, he'd tell me, by Webster, put it in the dictionary. It would. But that's where it originated from. Contrary to what Tommy Brown says about it, I know. I was there. That's where it originated. Uh-huh. I think that little fella, three years ago when I was in Chicago, with Sharky, I saw that same little Jewish guy, his old papers there. And he knows. He knows. He was in front of the lambs there? Yeah, on Clark Street, right on the corner. On Clark over there to look. Right on the corner. I went to look him up to see if he was still there. And he knows where the word jazz came from, too. Not 22nd Street.

Oh, yeah. Right downtown. So, Bert Swore and Charlie Mack came in there. And a fella named John Wilmess was the manager. So they told Johnny Wilmess that, where did you get this band from? That's according to a Charlie Mack statement. He said, oh, don't say anything about them. We're sending them back. So Mack says, well, you're crazy. He said, this is something different. He said, you don't understand what these guys are doing. He said, they're really crazy. My type of music. So those are the bamboo blackface comedian? Oh yeah, the first one, Sworn Mac, Sworn Mac before Moran and Mac. Yeah. And they were big time performers too, headliners. So they got up there and they asked us if we knew the yellow dog rag, and that was their, one of their big numbers. So they got up on the floor and we played the yellow dog rag,
and they sang it, and that was it. Well, they began packing it in there? Oh yes. Do you have any other big time people from the show that came over there? Oh, it was loaded every night. It got to be,
